Above, in pencil, T = closure{x'} and (T_y cap U) cup (T_y cap Z) subset T_y, written after the transcription (the last T_y is uncertain there; on the page it reads like a T with a curl). Left out: the boxed note and the struck words in the same margin, which belong to other lines of the page, and the word "de" right of the first formula. Still differs: the formulas are set in one line each, the hand is larger and slanted. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the last letter of the pencil formula is T_y: the union of (T_y cap U) and (T_y cap Z) is a subset of T_y, and the curl is the subscript y. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan on a unit grid and measured; not compiled (no TeX in the session). Changed: the two pencil formulas were centred 4 and 17 units right of the handwriting they set; each is now centred on it. The arrow x_1 -> x moved 1 unit left onto its ink, and the label X_y ∋ onto its letters. The node points, the three arrows of the triangle, the arrow y' -> y and the two dots lie on their ink to within about 1 unit; the formulas are typeset smaller than the hand, as with every label. Status set to ok.

drawings.description: croquis de la marge gauche, entouré d'une accolade avec $G_n$, $U_n$ ; les flèches entre $\hat{x}_1$, $\hat{x}'$ et $\hat{x}$ sont surchargées et ne sont pas reproduites ; un mot biffé suit « $\mathrm{Ass}\, \widehat{U}$ »

Hatted points x^_1, x^' in Ass U^, and x^ below. On the left G_n and U_n, and the long brace (pencil). The overinked arrows between the hatted points are not drawn, as in the transcription; the struck word after Ass U^ and a letter under U_n are left out. Still differs: the transcription has a plain arrow X_n -> X; on the page both X_n and Y_n have hooked strokes (drawn with hooks); G_n reads like G_{U_n} and U_n like U_{nn} on the page (labels after the transcription). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): X_n and Y_n are the infinitesimal neighbourhoods, closed subschemes of X and Y, so the hooked strokes (inclusions) drawn here are right and the transcription's plain arrow is not what the page has. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the upper label beside the brace reads G with the subscript U_n (the page's own diagram has i_{n*}(G_{U_n})), now drawn G_{U_n}; the lower one is U_n, its last strokes an overwriting; the transcription's G_n is to be corrected there. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the blot after Ass U^ is a word struck out with a heavy stroke; it stays left out. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan on a unit grid, corrected and measured; not compiled (no TeX in the session). Changed: the labels x_1, x', x, x^', Y_n, X_n, « ∈ Ass U^ » and « ⊃ U' » moved onto their letters (the last two had been set 4 and 8 units to the right); the arrows x_1 <- x', x_1 -> x and x' -> x moved 1 to 1.5 units left and up onto their ink; the short stroke X_n - Y_n moved 3 units left, under X_n, where it stands; the stroke y - y' moved 3 units left, between the two letters; the brace redrawn through its pencil, with its cusp at the height of X_n. Every stroke and label now lies on its ink to within about 1 unit. Status set to ok.

drawings.notes: Bottom of the page. Left column: points x', x; X' -> X; T' - T; T'_y - T_y (nodes placed once, each stroke on the line between the same two node points). The pencil notes written along the sheet ("U cap T_y dense dans T_y", "U cap T'_y dense dans T'_y", "T' = U T'_i", "T = U T_i") as rotated text, after the transcription. On the right, in ink: I^ (a small mark before it left out), I^ with a vertical = under it, then X^ cup {x} with a bar under {x} and a pencil oval round {x}, I^ under the bar, and eta^ to the left; placed as on the page, their articulation not legible, as the transcription says. The long pencil line crossing the right half is drawn faint. Left out: the formulas of the text above, cut by the crop. Still differs: the transcription puts T' -> T above X' -> X; on the page X' -> X is above T' - T, and T' - T has no visible arrowhead (see disagreement); the bar of "X^ cup closure{x}" is under {x} on the page. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): on the page X' -> X stands above T' -> T (the transcription has the other order), and a small faint arrow head is visible between T' and T; the arrow head is now drawn. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan on a unit grid, corrected and measured; not compiled (no TeX in the session). Changed: the pencil oval round {x} is larger and centred on its pencil (it lay 1 unit low and right and 1 unit short on every side); the lower I^ and the upper I^ of the right group moved onto their letters. The arrows and labels of the left group, the four pencil formulas (centred on their writing; the rasteriser of the check does not turn them, so their slant was checked by centre only), eta^, X^ ∪ {x} with its bar and the long pencil line lie on their ink to within about 1 unit. Status set to ok.

drawings.description: au bas de la page, six croquis de surfaces et de courbes : un carré coupé d'un trait vertical et d'une courbe ; une boîte surmontée d'une feuille en perspective, des droites par un point marqué ; une feuille que traversent une courbe et une droite par un point marqué, une courbe en tirets sur la feuille, et au-dessus un trait vertical à petite boucle ; deux feuilles en perspective marquées $Z'$, un point $\Phi'$ ; une feuille traversée d'une courbe épaisse ; une feuille dans une boîte, un trait épais sous $\Phi$, marquée $Z$
drawings.kind: six sketches of surfaces and curves (foot of the page)
drawings.notes: The six sketches of surfaces and curves at the foot of p. 19, redrawn stroke by stroke from the 400 dpi colour scan on gridded crops and overlaid on it (2026-11-13), in place of the whole-page redraw of 2026-11-09. The editor answered No to the question whether the six sketches matched the page in shape and order (#151), with the note « the top ones should read as latex diagrams, the drawings on the bottom should be … », cut at fifteen words by /review/. The diagrams at the top are therefore LaTeX in the transcription (the first tikz-cd and the square as before, the second now set in tikz-cd), and the redraw keeps only the sketches at the foot, redrawn closely from the page: that is how the cut end of the note is read (the sketches stay drawings, redrawn to match). Order as on the page, top row left to right: (1) a square cut by a vertical line and a curve, its upper left corner open; (2) a box, its bottom edge ending in an arrowhead, under a sheet in perspective; a horizontal and a vertical line and two oblique lines through a marked point, a heavy lens from the point to the right; (3) a sheet, its left edge thin above, a curve and a thin line through a marked point, a horizontal curve that reaches the point and runs on in dashes across the sheet and comes out beyond its right edge; above it a heavy vertical stroke with a small loop and a point, a thin hook at its top and a curve to the right; (4) at the right, Z' and two sheets in perspective, a point with a short curve through it, marked Phi'. Bottom row: (5) a sheet crossed by a heavy curve and a thin line through one point, its lower edge a long thin curve, a heavy dash at the right; (6) a sheet in a box, a heavy segment down from a point under Phi, Z at the right after a short dash. Faint strokes are drawn in pencil. Left out: the diagrams and formulas of the upper part of the page (in the transcription). Still differs: these are quick perspective drawings; the strokes lie within about half a millimetre of the page, but which stroke belongs to which surface is not always clear, in (2) and (6) especially. Not checked by a reader.
